Use this operation to test your access to this api.
If it responds with status 200, your access was successful.

post.description:
A lead consists of two fieldlists:
- prospect: A person or company along with contact information.
- interest: The formulated interest of the prospect.

A fieldlist is a collection of fields with an optional ordering, where each field consists of
- an identifier - the name of the field,
- a type, which describes syntax and semantic of the value,
- the value of the field, which is a string-representation conforming to the given type.

The field types are segmented in two classes:
- generic types, which only describe the syntax of the value (e.g. 'text:singleline' or 'number:natural')
- specific types, which additionally specify a semantic, on how to interpret the value (e.g. 'text:multiline:address')

get.description:
Use this operation to retrieve lists of leads that your company owns.\
The owner of a lead is the creator of it.

### Continuation
The amount of leads you can retrieve by a single request is limited.
You can iterate through all your leads using a continuation token which you get with every response header.
Use your previous query and add the returned continuation token to get the next set of results.
Once you get an empty result you know that there are no more leads available.

### Sorting
You may sort the results according to some sorting criteria in ascending or descending order.
You can also sort by multiple fields.

### Filtering
You may filter you list by some filter criteria.
The most common use case is to filter by modified leads since the last time you fetched modified leads. (Incremental updates)
- Example: GET /leads?modifiedAt=gte:2022-06-01

### FieldLists
By default this operation returns meta data and transactional data of leads.
So you will be able to tell when some lead has been modified as well as whether a lead has been won/lost or ist still in progress.\
If you are interested in the field lists of your leads as well, use the "includeFieldLists" query parameter!

### Commissions
A lead can be processed more than once — by several sales partners in turn or, with multi distribution, at the same time.
Every item carries the **newest** processing (by startedAt) as the flat "commission" object, exactly as before,
and additionally **all** processings of the lead as the "commissions" array, newest first, each element shaped like "commission".\
A lead that has never been processed has no "commission" and an empty "commissions" array.\
The array is additive and is being rolled out stage by stage; where it is not available yet, the field is absent.
Integrations that only read "commission" keep working unchanged.

parameters.name: includeFieldLists
parameters.description: Whether field lists of leads shall be returned.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description:
Sort results by one or multiple fields.\
\
Only the following fields are supported:
- modifiedAt
- lead.leadId
- lead.createdAt
- lead.modifiedAt
- commission.startedAt

If you want to sort by multiple fields, list them comma-separated.\
The sorting direction can by denoted by an (optional) '+' prefix for ascending order or a '-' prefix for descending order.
- Example 1: sort=-modifiedAt   (sort by modifiedAt descending)
- Example 2: sort=lead.createdAt,lead.leadId  (sort first by lead.createdAt ascending and second by lead.leadId ascending)

Hint: Special characters need to be URL-encoded in query strings. Like '+' (%2B).

parameters.name: modifiedAt
parameters.description:
Filter leads by field modifiedAt.\
The filter expression consists of an (optional) operator followed by a colon (":") and an ISO8601 date-time.\
\
Available operations:
- gte
- gt
- lte
- lt
- eq

Syntax: [operation]:value\
If operation is missing, then eq (equality) will be assumed.\
Supports multiple filter expressions.\
\
Examples:
- GET /leads?modifiedAt=2022-06-01
- GET /leads?modifiedAt=gte:2022-06-01
- GET /leads?modifiedAt=gte:2022-01-01&modifiedAt=lt:2023-01-1

get.description: Get a lead at its current state. (Consistently)

patch.description:
Modify the field lists of a lead. I.e. update contact information or add new/missing fields.\
Only field lists given in the request body will be modified. A field list will be updated with all it's fields as a whole.

post.summary: Commission a lead to a sales partner.
post.description:
This operation commissions the lead to the given sales partner directly.
It fails, if the lead has an active commission already. The operation is going to be dropped in future in favour of a new lead assignment mechanism to be announced.

salesPartnerId.description: Id of the sales partner to commission the lead to.

salesPipelineId.description: Id of the sales pipeline to use.

post.summary: Announce an attachment upload to a lead.
post.description:
Uploading a file as an attachment to a lead consists of two steps.

Step 1) Announce the upload. (This operation.)
Step 2) Upload the file using a multipart/form-data POST request to the 'uploadUrl' along with the 'fields' you received from the response of step 1.

See a code example on GitHub: https://github.com/leadtributor/examples/tree/master/attachment_upload

get.summary: Get duplicate candidates for a lead.
get.description:
Returns a list of leads that are potential duplicates of the given lead.
Each duplicate candidate contains a score between 0 (no match) and 100 (exact match)
as well as a list of matches describing which criteria triggered the duplicate detection.

### Matching criteria
- **email**: Exact, domain, and fuzzy email matching.
- **name**: Fuzzy matching on first and last name.
- **company**: Fuzzy company name matching.
- **location**: Geographic proximity matching.

parameters.name: maxDistanceKm
parameters.description: Maximum distance in kilometers for location-based duplicate matching. Leads further apart than this threshold receive no location score.

parameters.name: minScore
parameters.description: Minimum duplicate score (0–100) a candidate must reach to be included in the result.

leadId.description: Id of the potential duplicate lead.

leadName.description: Display name of the potential duplicate lead.

score.description: Duplicate confidence score. 0 = no match, 100 = exact match.

matches.description: List of criteria that contributed to the duplicate score.

field.description: The field on which a match was detected.

distanceKm.description: Distance in kilometers for location-based matches.

Sends an email invitation to a potential sales partner.
The invited party must accept the invitation before the partnership becomes active.

delete.description:
Permanently removes a sales partner record.
Only allowed when the partner status is ENDED, PENDING, or DECLINED.
To end an active partnership first, use POST /sales-partners/{id}/end.

post.summary: End an active sales partner relationship.
post.description:
Terminates an active partnership. The sales partner status changes to ENDED.
After ending, the record can be deleted via DELETE /sales-partners/{id}.

commissions.description:
All processings of the lead, newest first; each element is shaped like "commission", and the first one is
the same processing. Empty for a lead that has never been processed. Additive and rolled out stage by
stage — where not available yet, the field is absent.

uploadUrl.description: Upload url. Use this url to PUT your file to. This url is temporary and will expire in 5 minutes.

owner.description: Urn of the owner of the form.

responsible.description: Who has been commissioned/assigned to process the lead.

responsibleName.description: The name of who has been commissioned/assigned to process the lead.

step.description: The current step within the lead processing pipeline. (Zero indexed)

modifiedAt.description: Last modification of the lead processing.
